subproblem.title: Lipschitz extension of a map into ℝ^P with a √P loss (componentwise McShane)
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, S ⊆ ℝ^P (= Euclid P), ψ : ℝ^P → ℝ^P and K ∈ ℝ≥0 such that ψ is K-Lipschitz on S, i.e. |ψ(x) − ψ(y)| ≤ K|x − y| for all x, y ∈ S. Then there is φ : ℝ^P → ℝ^P which is (√P·K)-Lipschitz on all of ℝ^P (Lipschitz constant NNReal.sqrt P * K) and agrees with ψ on S.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (S : Set (Euclid P)) (ψ : Euclid P → Euclid P) (K : NNReal), LipschitzOnWith K ψ S → ∃ φ : Euclid P → Euclid P, LipschitzWith (NNReal.sqrt P * K) φ ∧ EqOn φ ψ S
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 3 of the parent proof (φ_r is the componentwise McShane extension of ψ|{d ≥ r}; Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.extend_real, mathlib/Mathlib/Topology/MetricSpace/Lipschitz.lean:308).
1. Coordinates. For i ∈ Fin P let ψ_i(x) := ψ(x) i ∈ ℝ. For every v ∈ ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) and every i, |v i| ≤ ‖v‖, because ‖v‖² = Σ_j |v j|² (EuclideanSpace.norm_eq). Hence for x, y ∈ S: |ψ_i(x) − ψ_i(y)| = |(ψ(x) − ψ(y)) i| ≤ ‖ψ(x) − ψ(y)‖ = dist(ψ(x), ψ(y)) ≤ K·dist(x, y). So LipschitzOnWith K ψ_i S (LipschitzOnWith.of_dist_le_mul).
2. Extension. By McShane's theorem (LipschitzOnWith.extend_real) there is g_i : ℝ^P → ℝ with LipschitzWith K g_i and EqOn ψ_i g_i S. Choose such a g_i for every i ∈ Fin P.
3. Definition. Let φ(x) ∈ ℝ^P be the vector whose coordinates are φ(x) i = g_i(x) (for example φ x := WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => g_i x), equivalently (WithLp.equiv 2 (Fin P → ℝ)).symm (fun i => g_i x)).
4. Agreement on S. If x ∈ S then φ(x) i = g_i(x) = ψ_i(x) = ψ(x) i for every i, so φ(x) = ψ(x) by extensionality of EuclideanSpace vectors. Thus EqOn φ ψ S.
5. Global Lipschitz bound. For all x, y ∈ ℝ^P, dist(φ(x), φ(y))² = Σ_i (g_i(x) − g_i(y))² (EuclideanSpace.dist_eq) ≤ Σ_i K²·dist(x, y)² = P·K²·dist(x, y)², because each g_i is K-Lipschitz. Both sides are nonnegative, so taking square roots gives dist(φ(x), φ(y)) ≤ √P·K·dist(x, y). Since the real number underlying NNReal.sqrt P * K is Real.sqrt P · K (NNReal.coe_mul, Real.coe_sqrt), LipschitzWith.of_dist_le_mul gives LipschitzWith (NNReal.sqrt P * K) φ. (For P = 0 the same computation gives dist(φ(x), φ(y)) = 0.)
6. Steps 4 and 5 are the two conclusions. ∎
proof_key_steps: Each coordinate ψ_i = ψ(·) i is K-Lipschitz on S since |v i| ≤ ‖v‖ in EuclideanSpace.
McShane (LipschitzOnWith.extend_real) extends each ψ_i to a globally K-Lipschitz g_i agreeing with ψ_i on S.
φ := the vector (g_i)_i agrees with ψ on S coordinatewise.
dist(φ x, φ y)² = Σ_i (g_i x − g_i y)² ≤ P K² dist(x,y)², so φ is (√P·K)-Lipschitz.

audit.reason: Coordinatewise McShane extension and the sum-of-squares estimate prove exactly the stated bound, including P = 0. Euclid uses PiLp 2, and the supplied WithLp construction selects the intended Euclidean metric.

subproblem.title: Markov selection of a good parameter in an interval
subproblem.statement: Let g : ℝ → [0, ∞] be almost-everywhere measurable for Lebesgue measure, p a predicate on ℝ that holds for Lebesgue-almost every t, a < b real numbers and I ∈ [0, ∞] with ∫_{(a,b)} g dL¹ ≤ I (lower Lebesgue integral over Ioo a b). Then there is t ∈ (a, b) with p(t) and (b − a)·g(t) ≤ 2·I, computed in [0, ∞] with b − a embedded by ENNReal.ofReal.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (g : ℝ → ℝ≥0∞) (p : ℝ → Prop) (a b : ℝ) (I : ℝ≥0∞), a < b → AEMeasurable g → (∀ᵐ t, p t) → ∫⁻ t in Ioo a b, g t ≤ I → ∃ t ∈ Ioo a b, p t ∧ ENNReal.ofReal (b - a) * g t ≤ 2 * I
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the parent proof (Markov's inequality on the interval (ρ_ν/2, ρ_ν) to pick a radius in the a.e. set of (SL2)). Notation: c := ENNReal.ofReal(b − a); since a < b we have 0 < c < ∞ and volume(Ioo a b) = c (Real.volume_Ioo). Write ν := volume.restrict (Ioo a b).
1. Suppose, for a contradiction, that the conclusion fails: for every t ∈ Ioo a b with p(t) we have 2·I < c·g(t) (push_neg).
2. Since p holds volume-a.e., for ν-a.e. t we have 2·I < c·g(t): by ae_restrict_iff' measurableSet_Ioo it suffices that for volume-a.e. t, t ∈ Ioo a b → 2·I < c·g(t), which follows from the a.e. statement for p and step 1 (filter_upwards).
3. A null-interval contradiction. If ∀ᵐ t ∂ν, False, then ν univ = 0 (ae_iff), i.e. volume(Ioo a b) = 0 (Measure.restrict_apply_univ), contradicting volume(Ioo a b) = c > 0.
4. Case I = ∞. Then 2·I = ∞ and ∞ < c·g(t) is impossible, so step 2 gives ∀ᵐ t ∂ν, False; contradiction by step 3.
5. Case I < ∞. By lintegral_mono_ae applied to the a.e. inequality 2·I ≤ c·g(t) of step 2: ∫⁻ t, 2·I ∂ν ≤ ∫⁻ t, c·g(t) ∂ν. The left side is 2·I·volume(Ioo a b) = 2·I·c (setLIntegral_const). The right side is c·∫⁻_{Ioo a b} g (lintegral_const_mul'' with the a.e.-measurability of g for ν, AEMeasurable.restrict), which is ≤ c·I by hypothesis. Hence 2·I·c ≤ c·I. As c ≠ 0 and c ≠ ∞ we may cancel c (ENNReal.mul_le_mul_right) and get 2·I ≤ I; since I < ∞ this forces I = 0 (for instance pass to toReal: 2x ≤ x with x ≥ 0 gives x = 0).
6. Then ∫⁻_{Ioo a b} g ≤ 0, so g = 0 ν-a.e. (lintegral_eq_zero_iff' with the a.e.-measurability of g for ν). With I = 0, step 2 says 0 < c·g(t) for ν-a.e. t; combining, for ν-a.e. t we get 0 < c·0 = 0, i.e. ∀ᵐ t ∂ν, False, contradicting step 3.
7. Both cases are contradictory, so some t ∈ Ioo a b satisfies p(t) and ENNReal.ofReal(b − a)·g(t) ≤ 2·I. ∎
proof_key_steps: Assume every t ∈ (a,b) with p(t) has 2I < (b−a)g(t); then this holds a.e. on (a,b).
If I = ∞ the a.e. inequality is impossible, so (a,b) would be null.
If I < ∞, integrating gives 2I(b−a) ≤ (b−a)∫g ≤ (b−a)I, hence I = 0.
With I = 0, g = 0 a.e. on (a,b) contradicts 0 < (b−a)g a.e.; so a good t exists.

audit.reason: The contradiction argument correctly handles I = infinity, finite positive I, and I = 0. Restriction of the a.e. hypotheses, cancellation of the finite positive interval length, and the zero-integral argument establish the exact conclusion.

subproblem.title: Mass of an integer multiplicity current concentrates on any closed set off which it vanishes
subproblem.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ, X ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ k) and R an IMRep in univ of degree k representing X. Let F ⊆ ℝ^P be closed such that X vanishes off F, i.e. X(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^P) whose tsupport is disjoint from F. Then μ_R(ℝ^P ∖ F) = 0 (R.measure Fᶜ = 0), and M(X) ≤ M_W(X) for every open W ⊇ F.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (X : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) k) (R : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) k) (F : Set (Euclid P)), R.Represents X → IsClosed F → (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) k, Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k)) (F) → X ω = 0) → R.measure Fᶜ = 0 ∧ ∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → F ⊆ W → X.mass ≤ X.massOn W
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 2 and 4 of the parent proof (μ_T(ℝ^P ∖ K) = 0 because admissible forms for the open set ℝ^P ∖ K have tsupport disjoint from K; the mass of a slice is carried by a neighbourhood of its level set). Dependency: (C1) = imrep_mass (Submission.dor_imrep_massOn_eq_measure_and_support), applied with U = univ.
1. By (C1) (univ is open and R represents X): X.massOn W = R.measure W for every open W ⊆ ℝ^P.
2. X.massOn Fᶜ = 0. By definition X.massOn Fᶜ is the supremum of ENNReal.ofReal(X ω) over ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn univ k Fᶜ. Every such ω has tsupport ω ⊆ Fᶜ, i.e. Disjoint (tsupport ω) F (Set.subset_compl_iff_disjoint_right), so X ω = 0 by hypothesis and ENNReal.ofReal 0 = 0. Hence the supremum is ≤ 0 (sSup_le), and it equals 0.
3. Fᶜ is open because F is closed, so step 1 gives R.measure Fᶜ = X.massOn Fᶜ = 0. This is the first conclusion.
4. Let W be open with F ⊆ W. Then Wᶜ ⊆ Fᶜ, so R.measure Wᶜ ≤ R.measure Fᶜ = 0. Using step 1 twice: X.mass = X.massOn univ = R.measure univ = R.measure (W ∪ Wᶜ) ≤ R.measure W + R.measure Wᶜ (measure_union_le) ≤ R.measure W + R.measure Fᶜ = R.measure W = X.massOn W. ∎
proof_key_steps: (C1): X.massOn W = R.measure W for open W.
Admissible forms for Fᶜ have tsupport disjoint from F, so X.massOn Fᶜ = 0 and hence R.measure Fᶜ = 0.
M(X) = R.measure univ ≤ R.measure W + R.measure Wᶜ ≤ R.measure W + R.measure Fᶜ = M_W(X).

audit.reason: Closedness makes the complement open, allowing C1 to turn vanishing test evaluations into zero complementary measure. Measure subadditivity then proves the stated localization inequality, without an unstated finiteness assumption.

subproblem.title: Zero and negated currents: integrality, mass of 0 − X, and the bound |X(ω)| ≤ sup|ω|·M(X)
subproblem.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ and U ⊆ ℝ^P open. (a) The zero current 0 ∈ 𝒟_k(U) is integer multiplicity. (b) If X ∈ 𝒟_k(U) is integer multiplicity then so is 0 − X (contract subtraction). (c) M_G(0 − X) = M_G(X) for every X ∈ 𝒟_k(U) and every G ⊆ ℝ^P. (d) If X ∈ 𝒟_k(U) with M(X) < ∞, ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U) and s > 0 with |ω(x)| ≤ s for all x (Euclidean coefficient norm covectorEuclideanNorm), then |X(ω)| ≤ s·M(X), where M(X) is read as a real number via ENNReal.toReal.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)), IsOpen U → IsIntegerMultiplicity (0 : GeometricCurrentOn U k) ∧ (∀ X : GeometricCurrentOn U k, IsIntegerMultiplicity X → IsIntegerMultiplicity (0 - X)) ∧ (∀ (X : GeometricCurrentOn U k) (G : Set (Euclid P)), (0 - X).massOn G = X.massOn G) ∧ ∀ (X : GeometricCurrentOn U k) (ω : TestFormOn U k) (s : ℝ), 0 < s → X.mass ≠ ∞ → (∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x) ≤ s) → |X ω| ≤ s * X.mass.toReal
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1 and 7 of the parent proof (the zero current is IM with empty carrier; M(0 − X) = M(X) because admissible forms are closed under negation; |T(ω)| ≤ M(T)·sup|ω| after scaling ω to be admissible). Dependency: im_calculus ((IMC)(c)).
1. (a) Define an IMRep R₀ in U with carrier ∅, mult ≡ 0 and orient ≡ 0. Its fields: ∅ is measurable and ∅ ⊆ U; CountablyRectifiable k ∅ by countablyRectifiable_of_measure_zero (μHE[k] ∅ = 0); the constant mult is measurable; mult_pos is vacuous; ∫⁻_{∅∩K} 0 dμHE[k] = 0 ≠ ∞; the constant orient is a.e.-strongly measurable; the orientation condition holds a.e. because μHE[k].restrict ∅ = 0. R₀ represents 0: 0(ω) = 0 and R₀.action ω = ∫_∅ … = 0. So 0 is IM.
2. (b) If X is IM, (IMC)(c) with A = 0 (IM by (a)) and B = X, on the open U, shows that 0 − X is IM.
3. (c) For ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U), (0 − X)(ω) = 0 − X(ω) = −X(ω) = X(−ω): the contract subtraction is pointwise and X.toCurrent is linear (map_neg). The map ω ↦ −ω sends massAdmissibleOn U k G into itself, because tsupport(−ω) = tsupport ω (tsupport_neg) and covectorEuclideanNorm((−ω)(x)) = covectorEuclideanNorm(−ω(x)) = covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(x)) (covectorEuclideanNorm_neg); it is an involution. Hence {ofReal((0 − X)(ω)) : ω admissible} = {ofReal(X(ω′)) : ω′ admissible} (ω′ = −ω), and taking suprema gives M_G(0 − X) = M_G(X).
4. Homogeneity of the coefficient norm: for c ∈ ℝ and a k-covector α, covectorEuclideanNorm(c·α) = |c|·covectorEuclideanNorm(α), since (c·α)(e_I) = c·α(e_I), the sum of squares is multiplied by c², and Real.sqrt(c²·S) = |c|·Real.sqrt(S).
5. (d) Let s > 0, M(X) < ∞ and |ω(x)| ≤ s for all x. Then ω′ := s⁻¹·ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U) (submodule), tsupport ω′ ⊆ tsupport ω ⊆ U and |ω′(x)| = s⁻¹|ω(x)| ≤ 1 (step 4), so ω′ and −ω′ are admissible for M(X) = M_U(X). By le_massOn, ofReal(X(ω′)) ≤ M(X) and ofReal(X(−ω′)) ≤ M(X); since M(X) < ∞ this gives X(ω′) ≤ M(X).toReal and −X(ω′) ≤ M(X).toReal (ENNReal.ofReal_le_iff_le_toReal). By linearity X(ω′) = s⁻¹X(ω), so |X(ω)| = s·|X(ω′)| ≤ s·M(X).toReal. ∎
proof_key_steps: The empty IMRep represents 0, so 0 is IM; (IMC)(c) gives 0 − X IM.
ω ↦ −ω preserves admissibility, so M_G(0 − X) = M_G(X).
covectorEuclideanNorm is absolutely homogeneous; ±s⁻¹ω are admissible, giving |X(ω)| ≤ s·M(X).

audit.reason: The empty representation proves zero integrality, subtraction calculus proves negation integrality, and negation preserves admissibility. Scaling by a strictly positive bound proves the evaluation estimate with the required finite-mass hypothesis.

subproblem.title: A good slice in a prescribed interval of levels (Markov choice of the slicing radius)
subproblem.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, T ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(ℝ^P) (domain univ) represented by an IMRep RT = (M, θ, ξ) in univ, RB = (M', θ', ξ') an IMRep in univ of degree m, f : ℝ^P → ℝ continuous, L ∈ ℝ≥0, P_t ∈ 𝒟_m(ℝ^P) for t ∈ ℝ, and real numbers a < b. Assume (H1) for every open W ⊆ ℝ^P, t ↦ M_W(P_t) is a.e.-measurable and ∫_ℝ M_W(P_t) dt ≤ L·M_W(T); (H2) for L¹-a.e. t: P_t is integer multiplicity, P_t vanishes off f⁻¹(t) (P_t(ω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω ∩ f⁻¹(t) = ∅), and P_t(ω) = ∫_{M∩{f<t}} θ⟨dω, ξ⟩ dH^{m+1} − ∫_{M'∩{f<t}} θ'⟨ω, ξ'⟩ dH^m for every ω ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P). Then there is t ∈ (a, b) such that P_t is integer multiplicity, P_t vanishes off f⁻¹(t), P_t satisfies the formula of (H2), and (b − a)·M(P_t) ≤ 2·(L·μ_RT({x : a < f(x) < b})) in [0, ∞] (b − a via ENNReal.ofReal, μ_RT = RT.measure).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (T : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1)) (RT : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1)) (RB : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m) (f : Euclid P → ℝ) (L : NNReal) (Ps : ℝ → GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m) (a b : ℝ), RT.Represents T → Continuous f → a < b → (∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → AEMeasurable (fun t => (Ps t).massOn W) ∧ ∫⁻ t, (Ps t).massOn W ≤ (L : ℝ≥0∞) * T.massOn W) → (∀ᵐ t, IsIntegerMultiplicity (Ps t) ∧ (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m, Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) m)) (f ⁻¹' {t}) → Ps t ω = 0) ∧ ∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m, Ps t ω = (∫ x in RT.carrier ∩ {x | f x < t}, (RT.mult x : ℝ) * RT.orient x (exteriorDerivative (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) m) x) ∂μHE[m + 1]) - ∫ x in RB.carrier ∩ {x | f x < t}, (RB.mult x : ℝ) * RB.orient x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) m) x) ∂μHE[m]) → ∃ t ∈ Ioo a b, IsIntegerMultiplicity (Ps t) ∧ (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m, Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) m)) (f ⁻¹' {t}) → Ps t ω = 0) ∧ (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m, Ps t ω = (∫ x in RT.carrier ∩ {x | f x < t}, (RT.mult x : ℝ) * RT.orient x (exteriorDerivative (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) m) x) ∂μHE[m + 1]) - ∫ x in RB.carrier ∩ {x | f x < t}, (RB.mult x : ℝ) * RB.orient x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) m) x) ∂μHE[m]) ∧ ENNReal.ofReal (b - a) * (Ps t).mass ≤ 2 * ((L : ℝ≥0∞) * RT.measure {x | a < f x ∧ f x < b})
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the parent proof (good radii, Simon (8)–(10) and 4.10), for the strip W = {a < f < b}. Dependencies: markov_point, im_concentrated, imrep_mass (C1).
1. W := {x | a < f x ∧ f x < b} = f⁻¹((a, b)) is open (isOpen_lt with f continuous, intersected).
2. By (H1) for this W, g(t) := M_W(P_t) is a.e.-measurable and ∫⁻ g ≤ L·M_W(T). By (C1) for T and RT (univ is open), M_W(T) = μ_RT(W). Put I := L·μ_RT(W). Then ∫⁻_{Ioo a b} g ≤ ∫⁻_ℝ g ≤ I (setLIntegral_le_lintegral).
3. Let p(t) be the conjunction in (H2): P_t is IM, P_t vanishes off f⁻¹{t}, and the formula holds for all ω. By (H2), p holds for a.e. t. Apply markov_point to g, p, a < b and I: there is t ∈ Ioo a b with p(t) and ENNReal.ofReal(b − a)·g(t) ≤ 2·I.
4. Fix this t. By p(t), P_t is IM, so some IMRep R_t in univ represents it, and P_t vanishes off F := f⁻¹{t}, which is closed (preimage of a point under the continuous f). Since a < t < b, F ⊆ W. By im_concentrated (X = P_t, R = R_t, F, and the open set W ⊇ F), M(P_t) ≤ M_W(P_t) = g(t).
5. Hence ENNReal.ofReal(b − a)·M(P_t) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(b − a)·g(t) ≤ 2·(L·μ_RT(W)) (monotonicity of multiplication in [0, ∞]), and W = {x | a < f x ∧ f x < b}. Together with p(t) this gives every clause of the conclusion. ∎
Remark: in the parent text the inequality M(P_t) ≤ M_W(P_t) is obtained with a smooth Urysohn cut-off; step 4 obtains the same inequality from (C1) through im_concentrated, which only needs that P_t is IM for the chosen t.
proof_key_steps: W = {a < f < b} is open and ∫_{(a,b)} M_W(P_t) dt ≤ L·M_W(T) = L·μ_RT(W) by (H1) and (C1).
markov_point gives t ∈ (a,b) in the a.e. set of (H2) with (b − a)·M_W(P_t) ≤ 2L·μ_RT(W).
P_t is IM and vanishes off the closed level set f⁻¹(t) ⊆ W, so im_concentrated gives M(P_t) ≤ M_W(P_t).

Source: step 2 of the parent proof (restrictions T⌞B represented by (M ∩ B, θ, ξ), their masses μ_T(B) by (C1), and their vanishing off K ∩ closure(B), using that M ∖ K is null). Dependencies: im_calculus ((IMC)(b) restriction and (IMC)(d) orientation bound), imrep_mass (C1), im_concentrated. Write M = R.carrier, θ = R.mult, ξ = R.orient, H^k = μHE[k], |α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α.
Part (A).
1. Let β be a test k-form and S := tsupport β (compact). x ↦ |β(x)| is continuous: it is Real.sqrt of a finite sum of squares of x ↦ β(x)(e_I), each continuous (continuous_eval_const composed with the continuous β). It vanishes off S (|0| = 0), so it has compact support (prove it with HasCompactSupport.mono' from the support of β) and is bounded: there is s ≥ 0 with |β(x)| ≤ s for all x (Continuous.bddAbove_range_of_hasCompactSupport).
2. By (IMC)(d), for H^k⌞M-a.e. x and every covector α, |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α|. Hence for H^k⌞M-a.e. x, |θ(x)·ξ(x)(β(x))| ≤ θ(x)·|β(x)| ≤ s·θ(x)·1_S(x), because β(x) = 0 for x ∉ S (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport).
3. The bound is integrable on M: ∫⁻_M s·θ·1_S dH^k = s·∫⁻_{M∩S} θ dH^k < ∞ by R.locallyIntegrable_mult with the compact set S ⊆ univ.
4. The integrand is a.e.-strongly measurable for H^k⌞M: θ is measurable, ξ is a.e.-strongly measurable (R.aestronglyMeasurable_orient), β is continuous, and evaluation (L, α) ↦ L(α) is a continuous bilinear map, so x ↦ ξ(x)(β(x)) is a.e.-strongly measurable. By Integrable.mono' the integrand is integrable on M. This proves (A).
Part (B).
5. By im_concentrated (X represented by R, F closed, X vanishes off F), R.measure Fᶜ = 0. Since R.measure = (H^k⌞M).withDensity θ and Fᶜ is measurable, R.measure Fᶜ = ∫⁻_{M∩Fᶜ} θ dH^k; as θ ≥ 1 on M (R.mult_pos, θ is ℕ-valued), H^k(M ∩ Fᶜ) ≤ ∫⁻_{M∩Fᶜ} θ dH^k = 0.
6. By (IMC)(b) (univ open, B measurable) there are Y ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^P) and an IMRep R′ in univ with R′.Represents Y, R′.carrier = M ∩ B, R′.mult = θ and R′.orient = ξ. So Y is IM (witness R′), and for every ω, Y(ω) = R′.action ω = ∫_{M∩B} θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)) dH^k (unfold IMRep.action and rewrite the three fields).
7. Mass. By (C1) for Y and R′, M(Y) = Y.massOn univ = R′.measure univ = ((H^k⌞(M ∩ B)).withDensity θ)(univ) = ∫⁻_{M∩B} θ dH^k. Also R.measure B = ((H^k⌞M).withDensity θ)(B) = ∫⁻_{B∩M} θ dH^k (withDensity_apply, Measure.restrict_restrict for the measurable B). As M ∩ B = B ∩ M, M(Y) = μ_R(B).
8. Vanishing. Let ω ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ∩ (F ∩ B) = ∅. For x ∈ (M ∩ B) ∩ F, x ∉ tsupport ω, so ω(x) = 0 and θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)) = 0. The rest, (M ∩ B) ∖ F ⊆ M ∩ Fᶜ, is H^k-null by step 5. Hence the integrand vanishes H^k⌞(M ∩ B)-a.e. (ae_restrict_iff', measure_mono_null) and Y(ω) = 0 (integral_eq_zero_of_ae). ∎
proof_key_steps: (A): |θ ξ(β)| ≤ θ·sup|β|·1_{spt β} a.e. on M by (IMC)(d), and ∫_{M∩spt β} θ < ∞ by local integrability; measurability from the IMRep fields.
im_concentrated gives μ_R(Fᶜ) = 0, hence H^k(M ∖ F) = 0 since θ ≥ 1 on M.
(IMC)(b) gives Y represented by (M ∩ B, θ, ξ); (C1) gives M(Y) = ∫_{M∩B} θ = μ_R(B).
If tsupport ω misses F ∩ B the integrand vanishes on M ∩ B ∩ F and M ∩ B ∖ F is null, so Y(ω) = 0.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 7 of the parent proof (Simon (19)–(21), (25): IM limits via (IMS), the identity T − Q = ∂R₁ + S₁, and lower semicontinuity of mass for M(∂Q)), and step 8 (vanishing of the limits). Dependency: zero_neg; (IMS) is the antecedent.
1. Finiteness: c·M(T) ≠ ∞ and c·M(∂T) ≠ ∞ (ENNReal.mul_ne_top), hence Σ_j M(V_j), Σ_j M(H_j) and Σ_j M(E′_j) are finite.
2. Q: (IMS) with U = univ, degree m + 1 and X_r = V_r gives an IM Q with HasSum (V_j(ω))_j (Q(ω)) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^{m+1} and M(Q) ≤ Σ_j M(V_j) ≤ c·M(T).
3. R₁: by zero_neg, 0 − H_j is IM and M(0 − H_j) = M(H_j), so Σ_j M(0 − H_j) = Σ_j M(H_j) < ∞. (IMS) in degree (m + 1) + 1 = m + 2 (instantiate its m with m + 1) gives an IM R₁ with HasSum ((0 − H_j)(η))_j (R₁(η)), i.e. HasSum (−H_j(η))_j (R₁(η)), for every η ∈ 𝒟^{m+2}, and M(R₁) ≤ Σ_j M(H_j) ≤ c·M(T).
4. S₁: in the same way with 0 − E′_j in degree m + 1: S₁ is IM, HasSum (−E′_j(ω))_j (S₁(ω)) for every ω, and M(S₁) ≤ Σ_j M(E′_j) ≤ c·M(∂T).
5. Currents of small mass are weakly small: if X_N ∈ 𝒟_{m+1} and M(X_N) → 0, then X_N(ω) → 0 for each ω. Indeed, ω is continuous with compact support, so there is s > 0 with |ω(x)| ≤ s for all x (the covector norm of ω is continuous with compact support — prove the compact support by HasCompactSupport.mono' — and Continuous.bddAbove_range_of_hasCompactSupport); M(X_N) < ∞ for large N; by zero_neg (d), |X_N(ω)| ≤ s·M(X_N).toReal, which tends to 0 (ENNReal.tendsto_toReal at 0); conclude by squeeze_zero_norm'. Apply this to A_N and to K_N.
6. Identity (21): fix ω ∈ 𝒟^{m+1} and put η := exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ (m+1) ω, so ∂H_j(ω) = H_j(η) and ∂R₁(ω) = R₁(η). As N → ∞ (HasSum.tendsto_sum_nat composed with N ↦ N + 1): Σ_{j≤N} V_j(ω) → Q(ω) (step 2); Σ_{j≤N} ∂H_j(ω) → −∂R₁(ω) (negate the HasSum of step 3 at η); Σ_{j≤N} E′_j(ω) → −S₁(ω) (step 4); A_N(ω) → 0 and K_N(ω) → 0 (step 5). Both sides of (h1) converge, so by uniqueness of limits Q(ω) − T(ω) + 0 + ∂R₁(ω) = −S₁(ω) − 0, i.e. T(ω) − Q(ω) = ∂R₁(ω) + S₁(ω).
7. Boundary mass (25), the lower semicontinuity argument written out for one admissible form: M(∂Q) is the supremum of ofReal(∂Q(ω)) over ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn univ m univ. For such ω, ∂Q(ω) = Q(dω) = lim_N Σ_{j≤N} V_j(dω) = lim_N Σ_{j≤N} ∂V_j(ω), and by (h2) Σ_{j≤N} ∂V_j(ω) = Σ_{j≤N} Y_j(ω) − L_N(ω). Now ofReal(Σ_{j≤N} Y_j(ω) + (−L_N(ω))) ≤ Σ_{j≤N} ofReal(Y_j(ω)) + ofReal(−L_N(ω)) (ENNReal.ofReal_add_le and Finset.le_sum_of_subadditive); ofReal(Y_j(ω)) ≤ M(Y_j) (le_massOn); ofReal(−L_N(ω)) = ofReal((0 − L_N)(ω)) ≤ M(0 − L_N) = M(L_N) (zero_neg (c)); and Σ_{j≤N} M(Y_j) ≤ Σ_j M(Y_j) ≤ c·M(∂T) (ENNReal.sum_le_tsum). So ofReal(Σ_{j≤N} ∂V_j(ω)) ≤ c·M(∂T) + M(L_N). Letting N → ∞ (continuity of ofReal; M(L_N) → 0), le_of_tendsto_of_tendsto' gives ofReal(∂Q(ω)) ≤ c·M(∂T); taking the supremum (sSup_le), M(∂Q) ≤ c·M(∂T). This is WeaklyConvergesOn.massOn_le_liminf for the partial sums, unrolled.
8. Vanishing: if tsupport ω ∩ F₁ = ∅ then V_j(ω) = 0 for every j, so HasSum (fun _ => 0) 0 and uniqueness of sums give Q(ω) = 0. If tsupport η ∩ F₂ = ∅ then (0 − H_j)(η) = −H_j(η) = 0 for all j, so R₁(η) = 0; likewise S₁(ω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω ∩ F₂ = ∅.
9. Steps 2–8 give all conclusions. ∎

Small mass implies small values (zero_neg (d)), so A_N(ω), K_N(ω) → 0; passing to the limit in (h1) gives T − Q = ∂R₁ + S₁.
For admissible ω, ∂Q(ω) = lim(Σ Y_j(ω) − L_N(ω)) ≤ c·M(∂T); hence M(∂Q) ≤ c·M(∂T).

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 6 of the parent proof (PF on each shell: identity, homotopy formula 2.25, linearity, locality, and the telescoping sums (S1), (S2)). Dependencies: im_calculus ((IMC)(c)), zero_neg. Conventions: id := (x ↦ x); all currents are on univ; (A − B)(ω) = A(ω) − B(ω) and 0(ω) = 0 hold by definition; currents with equal values are equal (GeometricCurrentOn.ext).
1. Lipschitz bookkeeping: id is Λ_j-Lipschitz because 1 ≤ Λ_j (LipschitzWith.id.weaken), and φ_j is Λ_{j+1}-Lipschitz because Λ_j ≤ Λ_{j+1} (LipschitzWith.weaken).
2. Images of 0. The zero current is IM (zero_neg (a)) and vanishes off every set. PF(2) with X = Y = 0, F = id, G = φ_j, E = E_j gives homot_m(id, φ_j, 0 − 0) = homot_m(id, φ_j, 0) − homot_m(id, φ_j, 0); as 0 − 0 = 0 (ext), evaluating at any ω gives homot_m(id, φ_j, 0)(ω) = 0. PF(2) with F = G = φ_j gives push_m(φ_j, 0)(ω) = 0 in the same way.
3. One-shell lemma. Fix j and IM currents X ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}, D′, Z′, Z″ ∈ 𝒟_m vanishing off E_j with ∂X(ω) = D′(ω) + Z′(ω) − Z″(ω) for all ω. Claim: (i) push_{m+1}(φ_j, X)(η) − X(η) − ∂homot_{m+1}(id, φ_j, X)(η) = homot_m(id, φ_j, D′)(η) + homot_m(id, φ_j, Z′)(η) − homot_m(id, φ_j, Z″)(η) for all η, and (ii) ∂push_{m+1}(φ_j, X)(ω) = push_m(φ_j, D′)(ω) + push_m(φ_j, Z′)(ω) − push_m(φ_j, Z″)(ω) for all ω. Proof: 0 − Z′ is IM (zero_neg (b)) and D′ − (0 − Z′) is IM ((IMC)(c)); ∂X = (D′ − (0 − Z′)) − Z″ as currents (ext and the pointwise formula), so ∂X is IM ((IMC)(c)); 0 − Z′ and D′ − (0 − Z′) vanish off E_j. PF(5) with k = m, Λ = Λ_j, (F, G) = (id, φ_j), E = E_j gives push_{m+1}(φ_j, X) − push_{m+1}(id, X) − homot_m(id, φ_j, ∂X) = ∂homot_{m+1}(id, φ_j, X), and PF(1) gives push_{m+1}(id, X) = X. Applying PF(2) to the pairs (D′ − (0 − Z′), Z″), (D′, 0 − Z′) and (0, Z′) (all IM and vanishing off E_j) expands homot_m(id, φ_j, ∂X) = (homot_m(id, φ_j, D′) − (homot_m(id, φ_j, 0) − homot_m(id, φ_j, Z′))) − homot_m(id, φ_j, Z″). Evaluating at η and using step 2 gives (i). For (ii), PF(5) with (F, G) = (φ_j, φ_j) gives ∂push_{m+1}(φ_j, X) = push_m(φ_j, ∂X); expand with PF(2) (F = G = φ_j) in the same way and use step 2.
4. Notation: V_j := push_{m+1}(φ_j, W_j), H_j := homot_{m+1}(id, φ_j, W_j), E′_j := homot_m(id, φ_j, D_j), Y_j := push_m(φ_j, D_j), K_j := homot_m(id, φ_j, Z_j), L_j := push_m(φ_j, Z_j).
5. Shell 0: step 3 with j = 0, X = W_0, D′ = D_0, Z′ = 0, Z″ = Z_0 (∂W_0 = D_0 + 0 − Z_0) together with step 2 gives V_0 − W_0 − ∂H_0 = E′_0 − K_0 and ∂V_0 = Y_0 − L_0 pointwise.
6. Shell j + 1: step 3 with j + 1, X = W_{j+1}, D′ = D_{j+1}, Z′ = Z_j, Z″ = Z_{j+1} (Z_j vanishes off E_j ⊆ E_{j+1}) gives V_{j+1} − W_{j+1} − ∂H_{j+1} = E′_{j+1} + homot_m(id, φ_{j+1}, Z_j) − K_{j+1} and ∂V_{j+1} = Y_{j+1} + push_m(φ_{j+1}, Z_j) − L_{j+1}.
7. Locality: PF(3) with Λ = Λ_{j+1}, E = E_j (compact), X = Z_j (IM, vanishing off E_j) and (F, G, F′, G′) = (id, φ_{j+1}, id, φ_j) gives homot_m(id, φ_{j+1}, Z_j) = homot_m(id, φ_j, Z_j) = K_j; with (F, G, F′, G′) = (φ_{j+1}, id, φ_j, id) it gives push_m(φ_{j+1}, Z_j) = L_j. (EqOn id id E_j is trivial, EqOn φ_{j+1} φ_j E_j is a hypothesis, and the four maps are Λ_{j+1}-Lipschitz by step 1.)
8. Telescoping: by induction on N, adding the shell-(N+1) identities of steps 6–7 to the identities for N (Finset.sum_range_succ applied only to the sums over range (N+1+1)), one gets Σ_{j≤N}(V_j − W_j − ∂H_j) = Σ_{j≤N} E′_j − K_N, which is (S1), and Σ_{j≤N} ∂V_j = Σ_{j≤N} Y_j − L_N, which is (S2); the base case N = 0 is step 5. ∎
proof_key_steps: Images of the zero current under push and homot vanish (PF(2) with X = Y = 0).
One-shell lemma: PF(1), PF(5) and three applications of PF(2) to ∂X = (D′ − (0 − Z′)) − Z″, with integrality from (IMC)(c) and zero_neg.
PF(3) identifies homot_m(id, φ_{j+1}, Z_j) = K_j and push_m(φ_{j+1}, Z_j) = L_j since φ_{j+1} = φ_j on E_j.
Induction on N telescopes the shell identities into (S1) and (S2).

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 5 of the parent proof (shells W_j = T⌞S_j, D_j = (∂T)⌞S_j with S_0 = {d ≥ r_0}, S_{j+1} = {r_{j+1} ≤ d < r_j}, items (a)–(d)) together with the identity ∂A_t = B_t + P_t of step 4. Dependency: im_restrict. Notation: M = RT.carrier, θ = RT.mult, ξ = RT.orient, M′ = RB.carrier, θ′ = RB.mult, ξ′ = RB.orient; for ω ∈ 𝒟^m put g_ω(x) := θ(x)ξ(x)((dω)(x)) (dω = exteriorDerivative ω) and h_ω(x) := θ′(x)ξ′(x)(ω(x)); for η ∈ 𝒟^{m+1} put k_η(x) := θ(x)ξ(x)(η(x)).
1. ∂T vanishes off K: if tsupport ω ∩ K = ∅ then tsupport(dω) ⊆ tsupport ω (tsupport_exteriorDerivative_subset), so ∂T(ω) = T(exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ m ω) = 0; the underlying form of exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ m ω is exteriorDerivative ω by definition.
2. Integrability: by im_restrict (A) for RT and RB, g_ω and k_η are integrable on M and h_ω on M′ (dω is a test form by exteriorDerivative_isTestForm).
3. Representations: T(η) = ∫_M k_η (RT represents T); hence ∂T(ω) = T(dω) = ∫_M g_ω; and ∂T(ω) = ∫_{M′} h_ω (RB represents ∂T).
4. Splitting (integral_inter_add_sdiff with the measurable sets {a ≤ f} and {f < b}; f is continuous, hence measurable): for G ∈ {M, M′}, u integrable on G and reals b ≤ a: (i) ∫_G u = ∫_{G∩{a≤f}} u + ∫_{G∩{f<a}} u, because G ∖ {a ≤ f} = G ∩ {f < a}; (ii) ∫_{G∩{f<a}} u = ∫_{G∩{f<b}} u + ∫_{G∩{b≤f<a}} u, because (G ∩ {f < a}) ∩ {f < b} = G ∩ {f < b} (as b ≤ a) and (G ∩ {f < a}) ∖ {f < b} = G ∩ {b ≤ f ∧ f < a}.
5. Construction (im_restrict (B)): with X = T, R = RT and F = K, let W_0 be the restriction to {r_0 ≤ f}, W_{j+1} the restriction to {r_{j+1} ≤ f ∧ f < r_j}, A_N the restriction to {f < r_N}; with X = ∂T, R = RB and F = K (allowed by step 1), let D_0 be the restriction to {r_0 ≤ f} and D_{j+1} the restriction to {r_{j+1} ≤ f ∧ f < r_j}. All these sets are measurable. Define W and D on ℕ by cases (W 0 = W_0, W (j+1) = W_{j+1}; likewise D). im_restrict gives: each W_j, D_j is IM; the integral formulas (e.g. W_0(η) = ∫_{M∩{r_0≤f}} k_η, D_0(ω) = ∫_{M′∩{r_0≤f}} h_ω, A_N(η) = ∫_{M∩{f<r_N}} k_η); the masses M(W_0) = μ_RT({r_0 ≤ f}), M(W_{j+1}) = μ_RT({r_{j+1} ≤ f < r_j}), M(D_0) = μ_RB({r_0 ≤ f}), M(D_{j+1}) = μ_RB({r_{j+1} ≤ f < r_j}), M(A_N) = μ_RT({f < r_N}); and each vanishes off K ∩ B for its set B.
6. Vanishing of W_j and D_j off E_j: for j = 0, K ∩ {r_0 ≤ f} = E_0; for j + 1, K ∩ {r_{j+1} ≤ f ∧ f < r_j} ⊆ E_{j+1}, so disjointness from E_{j+1} implies disjointness from that set (Disjoint.mono_right).
7. Boundary of W_0: ∂W_0(ω) = W_0(dω) = ∫_{M∩{r_0≤f}} g_ω = ∫_M g_ω − ∫_{M∩{f<r_0}} g_ω (4(i)) = ∂T(ω) − ∫_{M∩{f<r_0}} g_ω (step 3). Also D_0(ω) = ∫_{M′∩{r_0≤f}} h_ω = ∂T(ω) − ∫_{M′∩{f<r_0}} h_ω (4(i), step 3) and Z_0(ω) = ∫_{M∩{f<r_0}} g_ω − ∫_{M′∩{f<r_0}} h_ω (hypothesis). Therefore D_0(ω) − Z_0(ω) = ∂T(ω) − ∫_{M∩{f<r_0}} g_ω = ∂W_0(ω).
8. Boundary of W_{j+1}: r_{j+1} ≤ r_j (r antitone), so by 4(ii) ∂W_{j+1}(ω) = ∫_{M∩{r_{j+1}≤f<r_j}} g_ω = ∫_{M∩{f<r_j}} g_ω − ∫_{M∩{f<r_{j+1}}} g_ω and D_{j+1}(ω) = ∫_{M′∩{f<r_j}} h_ω − ∫_{M′∩{f<r_{j+1}}} h_ω. With the formulas for Z_j(ω) and Z_{j+1}(ω), D_{j+1}(ω) + Z_j(ω) − Z_{j+1}(ω) = ∫_{M∩{f<r_j}} g_ω − ∫_{M∩{f<r_{j+1}}} g_ω = ∂W_{j+1}(ω).
9. Partial sums, by induction on N: Σ_{j=0}^{N} W_j(η) = T(η) − A_N(η). For N = 0: W_0(η) = ∫_{M∩{r_0≤f}} k_η = ∫_M k_η − ∫_{M∩{f<r_0}} k_η = T(η) − A_0(η). For N → N + 1: Σ_{j≤N+1} W_j(η) = T(η) − A_N(η) + W_{N+1}(η) (Finset.sum_range_succ), and A_N(η) = ∫_{M∩{f<r_N}} k_η = ∫_{M∩{f<r_{N+1}}} k_η + ∫_{M∩{r_{N+1}≤f<r_N}} k_η = A_{N+1}(η) + W_{N+1}(η) by 4(ii).
10. Vanishing of Z_j off E_j, by induction on j; note E_j ⊆ E_{j+1} since r is antitone. If tsupport ω ∩ E_0 = ∅, then by step 7 Z_0(ω) = D_0(ω) − ∂W_0(ω), where D_0(ω) = 0 (step 6) and ∂W_0(ω) = W_0(dω) = 0 because tsupport(dω) ⊆ tsupport ω (step 6). If the claim holds for j and tsupport ω ∩ E_{j+1} = ∅, then by step 8 Z_{j+1}(ω) = D_{j+1}(ω) + Z_j(ω) − ∂W_{j+1}(ω) with D_{j+1}(ω) = 0, ∂W_{j+1}(ω) = W_{j+1}(dω) = 0 (step 6) and Z_j(ω) = 0 (induction hypothesis, since tsupport ω is disjoint from E_j ⊆ E_{j+1}).
11. Steps 5–10 give all conclusions. ∎
proof_key_steps: ∂T vanishes off K; all integrands are integrable (im_restrict (A)).
Shells, ∂T-shells and the sublevel pieces A_N are IM restrictions (im_restrict (B)) with the stated masses and vanishing sets.
Integral splitting along {f < r_j} gives ∂W_0 = D_0 − Z_0, ∂W_{j+1} = D_{j+1} + Z_j − Z_{j+1} and Σ_{j≤N} W_j = T − A_N.
Induction on j shows Z_j vanishes off E_j using these relations and E_j ⊆ E_{j+1}.
